name: upcoming-entry: a schedule entry decodes through the reduced calendar projection
description:
GetUpcomingSchedule renders app/views/api/schedules/calendar/_entry.json.jbuilder, not schedules/entries/_entry. That partial omits created_at, updated_at, title, inherits_status, parent and description_attachments — all @required on ScheduleEntry — narrows bucket to id + name, and adds `recurring`, which no other schedule-entry projection emits. Before #635 the operation declared ScheduleEntry anyway, so this body threw DecodingError.keyNotFound in Swift on bucket.type before it reached any of the six top-level omissions.

The dispatch fixes the window at 2026-06-01..2026-06-30 rather than reading it from the case: no mock runner consumes queryParams, and no assertion type can pin a query string (every runner records the path with the query stripped). Both bounds are @required, so the call cannot be made without them at all.

The runner returns a flat summary of the DECODED result — counts plus one scalar per reduced member — rather than the raw envelope. Two reasons: Go and TypeScript resolve a responseBody path as a top-level key only, so a nested assertion is not portable; and every value below is read back through the SDK's own model, so a decoder that dropped a member fails here instead of passing quietly.

name: upcoming-occurrence: a recurring occurrence carries recurring=true and date-only bounds
description:
The occurrences array is rendered by the SAME calendar entry partial, so it carries the same shape. What separates the two arrays is `recurring`: BC3 selects schedule_entries with recurrence_schedule IS NULL and the occurrences with it NOT NULL. name: upcoming-assignable: the item text is `content`, and a card carries no completion block
description:
app/views/api/schedules/calendar/_assignable.json.jbuilder emits `content` (recordable.title) — the retired Assignable schema declared `title`, so the one field callers want was permanently absent. `type` is the LOWERCASE short recordable name. Both elements here are real variants: a completed to-do carrying the partial's one conditional key (`completion`), and a card that omits it and whose completion_url is RELATIVE, because BC3 renders the non-to-do branch through bucket_step_completions_path — a _path helper, which emits no host.

name: upcoming-empty: an empty window is three empty arrays, not a missing key
description:
The half that always worked, pinned so the failure claim stays precise. #635 is NOT "fails on every live response": reports/schedules/upcoming/index.json.jbuilder writes all three keys unconditionally, so an empty window decodes under any contract. What failed was any window containing a schedule entry, a recurring occurrence or an assignable. All three arrays are @required, which is what this case pins — a body dropping one is a contract violation, not an empty result.
